# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the bomb beyond the existence of three cuttable wire positions, and no instructions have arrived yet. Cutting now would be unjustified, so I will wait for Mute’s manual information and Deaf’s visual observations.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visuals: display reads 0. Light is blue. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

Deaf’s visual report is audible to both me and Mute. Mute can apply the manual to those facts, but cannot speak the resulting wire number; Deaf can see Mute’s gestures and then say the result aloud to me. I am establishing a simple gesture code for Mute’s answer: thumbs-up means wire 1, OK sign means wire 2, thumbs-down means wire 3.

``` 
speak(text="Mute: apply the manual to Deaf's report. Signal your chosen cut using 👍 for wire 1, 👌 for wire 2, or 👎 for wire 3. Deaf: watch Mute and say the indicated wire number aloud to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow; light is now yellow.

The light has changed from blue to yellow, so Mute must use the current visual state when applying the manual. No gesture result from Mute has reached Deaf yet; because Deaf speaks after Mute each round, Deaf can relay Mute’s next gesture to me on the following turn. I will not cut until that relay arrives.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use the current state: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Please signal the manual's chosen wire with the agreed gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is now red. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The light is now red, so any earlier manual evaluation may no longer apply. I still have not received a relay of Mute’s gesture. Mute needs the latest visual state, and Deaf must explicitly translate Mute’s gesture into an audible wire number for me.

``` 
speak(text="Mute: recompute from current state: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow; then gesture the chosen wire (👍=1, 👌=2, 👎=3). Deaf: after seeing Mute's gesture, tell me aloud exactly: wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is now white. Display 0. Wires ordered blue, green, yellow.

The state continues to change each round, and Deaf still has not relayed any visible response from Mute. I need Mute to communicate the manual’s rule or answer in a form Deaf can relay, rather than rely on the previously proposed code alone. I will ask Mute to gesture the chosen wire using the agreed code and ask Deaf to report any gesture he sees, including if it is not one of those three symbols.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Current visuals are display 0, white light, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Apply the manual now. Gesture chosen wire: 👍=1, 👌=2, 👎=3. If the manual has a rule you need conveyed, gesture it or its answer clearly.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please report every gesture Mute makes, exactly by symbol if possible, and translate 👍 as wire 1, 👌 as wire 2, 👎 as wire 3. Current light is white.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is now green. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

I made an incorrect assumption: Deaf cannot hear my spoken instructions. Only Mute receives speech from me; Deaf can only receive gestures. Mute has been receiving Deaf’s visual updates, but no manual result has yet been relayed. Since the light changes every round, I should not cut from stale information. I will ask Mute to make the agreed visible choice gesture based on the latest report Mute has, and wait for Deaf to relay what Mute shows.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can only act after Deaf relays your visible choice. Based on the latest visual report you received, use the manual and make exactly one clear choice gesture: 👍 means cut 1, 👌 means cut 2, 👎 means cut 3. Repeat it each turn until acted on.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is blue again. Display 0; wires ordered 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

Deaf cannot hear my speech, so my earlier requests to Deaf did not reach him. Mute can hear me and can show a conventional number gesture that Deaf is likely able to identify and describe aloud. I will ask Mute to show the selected wire as a finger-number gesture, repeating it each turn; I will wait for Deaf’s audible observation.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use the latest visual state and manual. Show only the selected wire as a standard number gesture: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or the clearest available three-finger gesture for wire 3. Repeat it every turn until I cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Current visual state: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. For Blind: Mute previously gestured, in order across recent turns: thumbs-up, then thumbs-down, then OK sign.

Mute’s three visible choices were relayed only now, but they correspond to earlier states and cannot safely be applied to the current yellow light. Since Mute receives Deaf’s visual report one turn later, I need a choice explicitly tied to the visual state Deaf most recently reported. I will ask Mute to repeat the choice while identifying the light state it used with a two-gesture sequence, so Deaf can relay both on the next turn.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Do not rely on an unstated earlier state. For the latest state Deaf reported to you, gesture TWO symbols in order: first light code (👍=blue, 👎=yellow, 👌=red, ☝=white, ✌=green), then choice code (👍=cut 1, 👌=cut 2, 👎=cut 3). Repeat this pair each turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visual update: display 0; light red; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute just gestured: index finger raised (?).

The index-finger gesture is not yet an unambiguous cut instruction under the most recent two-symbol protocol: it may be the first, state-identifying symbol, and it does not match the yellow state Mute should have just received. I will not infer a wire from it. I will reset to a single fixed choice code and require Mute to repeat it, while Deaf can observe and relay it.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Reset protocol: ignore all earlier gesture schemes. Each turn, after receiving Deaf's latest visual report, apply the manual and gesture ONLY one of these: 👍 = cut wire 1; 👌 = cut wire 2; 👎 = cut wire 3. Repeat the same one-symbol answer until the next visual report changes the needed answer.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visual update: display 0; light white; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute just gestured: OK sign, then thumbs-down.

Mute’s reported gestures are still inconsistent with the latest one-symbol protocol: the OK sign and thumbs-down may be delayed parts of the earlier two-symbol scheme, rather than a current answer. Cutting on that ambiguity would be unsafe. I will keep the fixed choice code and ask Mute to give one symbol only, based on the latest visual report they received.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your last two gestures were ambiguous. Give exactly ONE symbol only, using the manual and the most recent visual state you received: 👍 means cut wire 1; 👌 means cut wire 2; 👎 means cut wire 3. No other gesture and no second symbol. Repeat that one symbol.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visual update: display 0; light green; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute just gestured: OK sign.

Mute’s single OK sign follows the reset protocol and therefore means cut wire 2. However, it was calculated from the most recent report Mute had received (white), while Deaf has now reported a changed green light. The choice may no longer be valid, so I will wait for Mute’s answer based on green rather than cut on stale state.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Light has changed to green. Apply the manual to green when you receive this update, then give exactly one symbol only: 👍=cut 1, 👌=cut 2, 👎=cut 3.")
wait()
```
